program: NSF Designing Materials to Revolutionize and Engineer our Future (DMREF), NSF 25-508
direction: Materials-by-design: accelerating discovery of solid-state electrolytes for next-generation batteries
title: Closed-loop theory-computation-experiment design of solid-state electrolytes for safe, high-energy solid-state batteries
background: Solid-state batteries promise higher energy density and improved safety over conventional lithium-ion cells, but their deployment is bottlenecked by the lack of solid electrolytes that simultaneously deliver high ionic conductivity, wide electrochemical stability windows, low interfacial resistance and mechanical robustness. Discovery has historically proceeded by slow, largely empirical trial-and-error. Consistent with the Materials Genome Initiative, this project will accelerate the path to deployment by tightly coupling theory, high-throughput computation, machine-learning-guided candidate selection, and targeted synthesis/characterization in an iterative closed loop, so that computation guides which materials and interfaces are made and measured, and experimental feedback continually refines the models. The goal is a validated design framework and a set of candidate solid electrolytes with quantified, co-optimized transport, stability and mechanical properties.
challenges: Co-optimizing conflicting property targets: high ionic conductivity often trades off against electrochemical/mechanical stability, requiring multi-objective design rather than single-property screening
Predicting and engineering buried interfaces: electrolyte-electrode interfacial resistance and reactivity are hard to model and measure yet dominate cell performance

Closing the computation-experiment loop efficiently: integrating high-throughput DFT/ML predictions with synthesis and characterization under an active-learning strategy that minimizes costly experiments
FAIR data and transferable models: generating, curating and sharing datasets and models that generalize across chemistries rather than overfitting to a narrow family
sponsor: U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), Division of Materials Research

budget.note: DMREF awards are $1,500,000–$2,000,000 total over a duration of four years; this task uses the $2,000,000 / 48-month upper bound. NSF anticipated ~25 awards for the solicitation, subject to availability of funds.

eligibility: Proposals may be submitted by Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs) accredited in and having a campus located in the US. Each proposal must be led by a team of at least two Senior Personnel with complementary expertise. No individual may appear as Senior Personnel on more than one DMREF proposal in the competition.
requirements: Employ an iterative, closed-loop approach in which theory guides computation, computation guides experiment, and experimental results refine theory/computation
Include a Data Management Plan responsive to the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) guidelines
Make digital data generated by the project freely and openly available within a reasonable time
constraints: Total budget must fall within $1,500,000–$2,000,000 over four years
Team must include at least two Senior Personnel with complementary expertise spanning synthesis/processing, characterization, theory/computation and data science
Eligible submitting organizations are US-based IHEs
